payload.name: Search engagement events for favorite-item questions
payload.description: When a question asks for a person's favorite or preferred item and explicit favorite/preference memories are missing, search for recent or current engagement with that item category and treat event memories naming a specific item as evidence.
content: If a favorite/preference question (e.g., favorite video game, book, movie, food) yields no explicit favorite memory, run an additional search using the person's name and the item category without the word 'favorite' (e.g., '<name> video game', '<name> book'), including both 'event' and 'preference' memory kinds.

Inspect any event memories describing the person currently playing, reading, watching, eating, or recommending a specific item; a specifically named item in an ongoing or recent activity can support the answer even if the memory does not use the word 'favorite'.
When judging evidence sufficiency for such questions, a memory of current engagement with a concrete item may be sufficient if no other specific item is named.

solves: A favorite/preference question can fail when memory stores the item only as an event (e.g., currently playing, recommending) without the word 'favorite'. This skill applies to future questions asking for a person's favorite or preferred item in any category; it instructs retrieval to also search engagement events and treat a specifically named engaged item as evidence when no explicit preference exists.
